executiveSummary: Voice-enabled social engineering remains the most consequential synthetic-media threat this cycle, with multiple high-urgency incidents leveraging convincing phone or platform-based calls to obtain access, deliver malware, or defraud victims. Recent cases include large-scale passkey enrollment vishing targeting enterprise accounts, malware pushed via impersonated IT-support calls on collaboration platforms, criminal caller-ID spoofing capabilities linked to 1.8 million scam calls, and a high-value consumer loss in Hong Kong attributed to AI-generated voice notes. View Article View Article View Article View Article Regulatory transparency requirements for synthetic content are advancing in the European Union, where operational guidance for AI Act obligations is now in effect for the marking and disclosure of AI-generated or manipulated media, with Article 50 detailing applicable controls. View Article Security Advisory Defensive developments center on provenance and watermarking: the C2PA 2.3 specification expands support for text and fine-grained actions; research proposes privacy-preserving redaction of provenance data; and new work explores watermarking of embedding vectors bound to C2PA. Vendor Advisory Supporting Report Supporting Report Given concurrent criminal misuse of voice impersonation and expanding disinformation and policy gaps in election contexts, alongside active but still maturing defenses, the overall threat environment appears to be worsening. Identity workflows: Require out-of-band confirmation and manager approval for new passkey enrollments, MFA resets, and privilege grants. (Analyst Recommendation)
Telephony authenticity: Enforce call-back procedures to verified internal numbers; block/flag high-risk caller-ID anomalies; leverage STIR/SHAKEN analytics where available. (Analyst Recommendation)
Collab platforms: Restrict external calling permissions; enable recording/retention for security investigations; alert on links/executables in proximity to voice calls. (Analyst Recommendation)
Consumer protection: Promote shared "safe words" or code phrases for urgent financial requests over voice or messaging. (Analyst Recommendation)
Provenance controls: Pilot C2PA signing for high-risk media workflows; test privacy-preserving redaction to protect sensitive capture metadata. (Analyst Recommendation)
Forensics: Preserve original audio, call metadata, and platform logs; examine prosody/timbre artifacts and temporal inconsistencies indicative of synthesis. (Analyst Recommendation)
Awareness & training: Run vishing tabletop exercises with helpdesk, finance, and exec staff; incorporate deepfake voice exemplars. (Analyst Recommendation)
